links.description: ADR-0142 is a published Redwood architecture decision record in the architecture-and-standards Confluence space.
The serving runtime belongs to Redwood and changes frequently via kernel, scheduler, model config, GPU fleet updates and staged rollouts.
The production performance canary is Redwood's always-on canary for per-model serving performance.
Canary detects p95 latency regressions and throughput drops early in the serving runtime and gives attribution signals (kernel vs scheduler vs infra).
links.conditions: Must avoid paging on expected variance and baseline drift such as slow fleet mix changes or regional differences.

links.description: ADR defines how the perf canary computes baselines, regression thresholds, minimum sample sizes and anti-flap/dedupe logic.

Metrics/Baselines is a Redwood engineering team.
SRE is a Redwood team handling on-call and threshold standards.
Serving Runtime is a Redwood team that triages runtime warnings.
Release Engineering is a Redwood team involved in rollout gating.
Logan Wright is the named owner for Telemetry Platform in the ownership appendix.
Nadia Rahman is the named owner for Metrics/Baselines in the ownership appendix.

Telemetry Platform jointly owns the baseline pipeline and baseline artifact integrity.
Metrics/Baselines jointly owns the baseline pipeline and baseline artifact integrity.
The baseline pipeline generates the fixed baseline artifacts whose integrity Telemetry Platform and Metrics/Baselines own.
SRE owns threshold standards and paging hygiene for the perf canary.
Serving Runtime owns the list of models covered by the canary.
Serving Runtime co-owns the rollout gating integration with Release Engineering.
Release Engineering co-owns the rollout gating integration with Serving Runtime.
The ADR's decision is a hybrid baseline strategy combining a fixed primary baseline with a rolling secondary health baseline.
Driver 1: warnings must be useful and pages rare and high-confidence.
Driver 2: regressions should be detected quickly for top models in covered regions.
links.conditions: Applies to top models in covered regions.

links.description: Driver 3: baseline keys must match root-cause dimensions: runtime build, kernel tags, SKU.
Driver 4: SRE/on-call need a predictable reading of regression vs baseline, including during ongoing rollouts.
Driver 5: avoid alert storms from baseline drift, delayed metric ingestion and label cardinality errors.
Primary baseline is a fixed, versioned baseline per model key, used for rollout gating and paging.
links.conditions: Optional region override per key.

links.description: Secondary baseline is a rolling health baseline for drift monitoring and threshold calibration only.
links.conditions: Not used for paging.

links.description: Hybrid strategy includes rules that freeze or pause baseline updates during rollouts and incidents.
Threshold evaluation requires min sample size, sustained breach across multiple windows, and hysteresis.
Fixed baselines are stored per model, model_version, runtime_build, kernel_set_id and hardware_sku so comparisons stay like-for-like.
links.conditions: Region override optional.

links.description: Fixed baselines come from controlled perf-canary runs at prod-like load using the approved synthetic prompt distribution.
Fixed baselines are stored as immutable artifacts in a versioned store.
Fixed baseline is the reference for rollout gating.
Fixed baseline is the reference for paging decisions.
Each baseline key stores p50/p95/p99 summaries per latency metric, mean and std dev where stable, and run metadata (time range, sample count, canary config version).
links.conditions: Mean/std dev only where stable enough to be meaningful.

links.description: Each baseline key stores tokens/sec distribution summaries.
A fixed baseline is valid only if it meets minimum sample sizes and passes sanity checks.
links.conditions: Sanity checks: no telemetry gaps and no error-rate spikes.

links.description: Fixed baseline is stable and easy to reason about during rollouts but can go stale as hardware/driver stacks and workloads evolve.
Rolling baseline adapts over time but may drift and mask regressions or create false positives when drift is misread as regression.
Rolling health baseline uses recent stable periods with daily aggregates and median-of-daily-p95 robust statistics to dampen short spikes.
links.conditions: Excludes periods marked as rollout or incident.

links.description: Rolling baseline never auto-suppresses a fixed-baseline regression; it serves only as a triage and tuning signal.
Rolling baseline detects slow drift (e.g., fleet changes) that may justify generating a new fixed baseline.
links.conditions: When slow environmental drift is detected.

links.description: Rolling baseline suggests region or SKU overrides when variance is consistently higher.
links.conditions: When variance is consistently higher for a region/SKU.

links.description: During a runtime rollout the alert baseline is frozen to the latest fixed baseline for the active runtime build on that ring.
links.conditions: Applies while a runtime rollout is in progress on the ring.

links.description: Freeze rule is triggered by canary/gradual runtime rollouts.
When a perf regression incident is declared, baseline updates stop for affected keys.
links.conditions: Only for keys affected by the declared incident.

links.description: model_id (canonical model identifier) is a required baseline key field in v1.
model_version (registry version/hash) is a required baseline key field.
runtime_build_id (serving runtime build tag) is a required baseline key field.
kernel_set_id (kernel selection/version id) is a required baseline key field.
hardware_sku is a required baseline key field, e.g. H100-80GB or A100-80GB.
Region is an optional key field for regions with materially different fleet/network characteristics.
links.conditions: Only when variance requires it.

links.description: capacity_tier (hosted vs dedicated pools) is an optional key field.
links.conditions: Only when pools differ materially.

links.description: Baselines are never keyed by customer, endpoint, or prompt content due to privacy and cardinality constraints.
Scheduler flags that materially change behavior must appear in runtime_build_id or an explicit scheduler_profile tag.
links.conditions: scheduler_profile introduced only if needed; off by default to control cardinality.

links.description: Canary computes baselines and regressions for end-to-end latency at p50, p95 and p99 in ms.
Canary tracks runtime-only latency p50/p95/p99 in ms, excluding network/client.
Canary tracks prefill latency in ms.
Canary tracks decode latency in ms.
Canary tracks scheduler-level queueing time in ms.
Canary tracks overall tokens/sec and decode tokens/sec.
links.conditions: Decode tokens/sec only where available.

links.description: Canary tracks batch size distribution to aid attribution.
Canary tracks KV cache hit rate as an informational metric in v1.
links.conditions: Only where applicable.

links.description: Regression = meaningful deviation from fixed baseline; per metric, key and window compute percent change of observed vs baseline value.
links.conditions: Guarded by minimum samples and sustained breach.

links.description: Percent thresholds chosen because models differ in absolute latency; p95 is the primary SLO-relevant tail metric.
Warnings are actionable signals for runtime team triage and are sent to #eng-runtime.
Warning alerts are for the runtime team to triage.
Paging alerts for sustained, high-confidence regressions on top models go to the on-call rotation.
links.conditions: Only top models; sustained and high confidence.

links.description: Thresholds are configurable per model; platform defaults apply unless overridden in canary config.
links.conditions: Defaults used unless a per-model override exists.

links.description: Default warning when p95 E2E latency rises vs baseline in 2 of 3 consecutive windows.
links.conditions: Min samples met; per-model override may change it.

links.description: Default page when p95 E2E latency rises vs baseline in 3 of 4 consecutive windows.
links.conditions: Min samples met; top models only; per-model override may change it.

links.description: Default warning when tokens/sec drops vs baseline in 2 of 3 windows.
links.conditions: Min samples and min token count met.

links.description: Default page when tokens/sec drops vs baseline in 3 of 4 windows.
links.conditions: Min samples and min token count met; top models only.

links.description: Queueing p95 rise is a non-paging attribution signal suggesting scheduler/fleet saturation, shown on dashboards and in payloads.
links.conditions: Does not page unless explicitly enabled for a model.

links.description: Prefill p95 rise is a non-paging signal hinting at kernel/model config regressions.
links.conditions: Does not page unless explicitly enabled for a model.

links.description: Decode p95 rise is a non-paging signal hinting at kernel/model config regressions.
links.conditions: Does not page unless explicitly enabled for a model.

links.description: Runtime-only attribution signals (queueing, prefill, decode) are included in alert payloads.
Paging relies on customer-impact proxies (E2E p95 and tokens/sec) because breakdown metrics are noisier and sensitive to load mix.
Canary evaluates windows continuously with a default window length, subject to sustained breach rules.
Latency metrics need a minimum number of successful canary requests per key per window.
links.conditions: Per key K, per window.

links.description: Tokens/sec needs both a minimum request count and minimum generated token volume per key per window.
links.conditions: Both conditions required (AND).

links.description: If sample requirements are unmet, no alert state change is allowed, preventing flapping in low-coverage periods.
links.conditions: Triggered when per-window sample requirements are not met; applies to warning and paging.

links.description: Dashboards show an insufficient sample annotation when minimums are not met.
links.conditions: When sample requirements are not met.

links.description: Tail latency (p95/p99) is unreliable at small N; tokens/sec needs token volume to smooth per-request variance.
Warning requires breaches in M-of-N consecutive windows to resist transient spikes.
Paging requires breaches in M-of-N consecutive windows.
Warning clears only after performance returns closer to baseline on both latency and tokens/sec for all of 3 windows.
links.conditions: Both latency and tokens/sec conditions must hold.

links.description: Paging clears only after recovery closer to baseline on latency and tokens/sec for all of 4 windows.
links.conditions: Both latency and tokens/sec conditions must hold.

links.description: After a warning fires, a cooldown applies before a new incident thread is opened for the same key.
links.conditions: Per same key after transition to firing.

links.description: After a page fires, a longer cooldown applies before re-triggering a new incident thread for the same key.
links.conditions: Per same key after transition to firing.

links.description: Incident-bot dedupes alerts on model, version, runtime build, kernel set, SKU, optional region, metric type and severity.
links.conditions: Region included only if present.

links.description: If telemetry ingestion is delayed too long, alert evaluation is suspended.
links.conditions: Triggered when ingestion delay exceeds 2x evaluation window.

links.description: Telemetry delay protection emits a separate telemetry delay warning.
links.conditions: Ingestion delay > 2x window.

links.description: Telemetry delay warnings are sent to #eng-platform.
Pure rolling baseline adapts to drift but can mask slow regressions, makes gating moving goalposts, and risks alert storms from label bugs or ingestion gaps.
links.conditions: Rejected for paging/gating; allowed only as secondary calibration signal.

links.description: Pure fixed baseline is stable but goes stale with fleet/hardware/driver changes, raising false positives and manual work.
links.conditions: Adopted as primary baseline with explicit regeneration workflows.

links.description: The fixed-baseline alternative was folded into the hybrid strategy as the primary baseline.
Rolling approach survives only as secondary calibration signal.
Always-on per-region baselines reduce cross-region false positives but cause baseline explosion and operational overhead.
links.conditions: Region keys enabled only for models/regions where observed variance requires it.

links.description: Stable versioned baselines support rollout gates and high-confidence paging; rolling baseline adds drift visibility without hurting safety.
Anti-flap controls cut alert noise and prevent incident-bot storms.
Tradeoff: new baseline artifacts must be generated whenever major runtime/kernel changes land for covered models/SKUs.
links.conditions: Triggered by major runtime or kernel changes for covered models/SKUs.

links.description: Tradeoff: some true regressions are caught slightly later because of sustained-breach requirements.
Tradeoff: optional region/tier overrides add complexity when enabled.
links.conditions: Only when overrides are enabled.

links.description: Baseline artifact store must be access-controlled, versioned and auditable, recording who created artifacts and when.
Canary config must allow per-model thresholds by severity and whether region-specific keys are enabled.
Canary config must carry a per-model top model flag.
The top model flag determines whether a model is eligible for paging.
links.conditions: Only top-flagged models can page.

links.description: Alert payloads must carry observed value, baseline value, percent change, sample counts and token counts.
Alert payloads must include runtime_build_id, kernel_set_id, hardware_sku and region.
Alert payloads must link to dashboards, traces and the runbook.
Alert payloads must link to perf dashboards.
Changes to default thresholds need an ADR update or an SRE-approved change request.
links.conditions: Applies to platform default thresholds.

links.description: Alternative path for changing default thresholds is updating this ADR.
Phase 1 runs the canary in a single region with warnings only, tuning per-model overrides until noise is acceptable.
links.conditions: Exit when noise is acceptable.

links.description: Phase 2 turns on paging only for top models with proven low variance and stable baselines.
links.conditions: Only top models with proven low variance and stable baselines.

links.description: Phase 1 (warnings only) comes before Phase 2 (paging for top models).
Phase 2 comes before Phase 3 gating integration.
Phase 3 integrates canary gating with release engineering; warning acts as soft fail and paging as hard fail.
links.conditions: Only once the paging signal is trusted.

links.description: Rollout gating uses warning as early soft fail and paging as hard fail.
links.conditions: Paging signal must be trusted first.

links.description: Whether to add scheduler_profile to baseline keys, trading cardinality against attribution benefit.
links.conditions: Tracked outside the ADR.

links.description: Open question whether to page on runtime-only p95 for some enterprise-dedicated pools where E2E has extra network variance.
links.conditions: Tracked outside the ADR.

links.description: The runtime-only paging question targets certain enterprise-dedicated pools.
Open question whether to add a lightweight statistical test such as bootstrap CI on p95 for unusually high-variance models.
links.conditions: Only for models with unusually high variance; tracked outside the ADR.

links.description: Illustrative customer-critical top model pages at tighter thresholds and a stricter minimum token count.
links.conditions: Illustrative only.

links.description: Illustrative high-variance model is warning-only with wider thresholds and region-specific baseline enabled.
links.conditions: Illustrative only; no paging.

links.description: Illustrative new-kernel candidate gets a temporarily tighter warning during the rollout ring; paging stays default.
links.conditions: Paging remains at default until validated; illustrative only.

links.description: The tighter warning override is tied to the rollout ring of a new kernel candidate.
Changelog entry clarified cooldown timers.
Changelog entry added the telemetry delay protection rule.
Changelog entry tightened the tokens/sec minimum token count requirement.
The 2026-02-12 change is recorded in the ADR changelog.
